newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia shares down sharply, end off lows.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia shares down sharply, end off lows.

text.p: Leading Russian shares dived on Tuesday over investors' concern about President Boris Yeltsin's health but ended off their lows after a late rise, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 6.16 percent to 157.16 on a relatively high $23.64 million in volume.
"The difference in Friday and Tuesday prices was too big for buyers not to appear," said Andrei Kukk, chief trader at Rinaco-Plus brokerage. But he added that sell orders still outweighed buy orders.
Speculation that Yeltsin's health is worse than previously supposed, opening up the possibility of a lengthy period of political instability, hit shares on Monday.
Prices fell further on Tuesday. The market opened with panic selling and some shares fell by about as much as seven percent.
The surgeon likely to lead the surgery on Yeltsin's heart said on Tuesday there was no chance of the surgery being cancelled. He said on Sunday there was such a possibility.
"In the afternoon the market calmed down and the news only added to the tranquility," Kukk said.
Yeltsin's spokesman said a team of doctors, including U.S. specialist Michael DeBakey, will meet Yeltsin at around 0800 GMT on Wednesday to discuss a possible date for the operation.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said there could be no talk at present of Yeltsin resigning for health reasons, something urged by the communist opposition.
Kukk said prices would have fallen anyway even without the latest concerns about Yeltsin.
"Historically the market falls in the winter here and I do not see anything to change the tradition," he said.
He said that the volume of sell orders was likely to be up to twice the volume of buy orders for the next few months.
Kukk said prices would rise in the next couple of days, continuing to correct this week's fall, but they would still be lower than Friday opening quotes.
"Now the smartest Western investors are trying not to miss the chance and buy cheap papers," said Maksim Perlin, a trader from UFG.
Mosenergo was traded at $0.832 after $0.887 at Monday's close, UES fell to $0.0716 from $0.0732, Rostelekom edged down to $2.20 from $2.36 and LUKoil fell to $8.62 from $8.95.
